SHAKA ILEMBE - A LEGENDARY PRODUCTION

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we get a behind the scenes peak of MNET's epic new local series - SHAKA ILEMBE.

Unique Selling Point:
* MNET COLAB
* HUGE LOCAL INTEREST
* STAR STUDDED SHOW

Summary:
Shaka Ilembe airs in June this year - we speak to the brains behind an epic production - bringing to life a part of South African history on a Hollywood Scale.

Further information:
One on One interviews with MNET's CEO Nomsa Philiso, Executive Producer & Hollywood star, Nomzamo Mbatha and Desiree Markgraaff for Shaka Ilembe.

These three power house women - give our viewers insight into what it takes to tell a South African story that is everything a blockbuster is made of.

Script:


SHAKA ILEMBE

NOMSA: // There's love,
NOMSA: the tears
UPSOUND VAN TRAILER

NOMSA: It's everything,
UPSOUND VAN TRAILER

DESIREE: // epic drama,
UPSOUND VAN TRAILER
DESIREE: // big epic battle scenes.

UPSOUND VAN TRAILER

NOMZAMO: It is a story that's going to mean so much to so many for a very long time.

VO: Six years in the making, this is the origin story of Shaka Zulu.

UPSOUND TRAILER SEQUENCE… START DESIREE CIP UNDER…

DESIREE: // We feel the weight and the importance of the story.
VO: Multi-award winning film maker, Desiree Markgraaff, is one of the executive producers behind this world-class production.

DESIREE: there's a lot about the story of King Shaka that has never been told.// We were interested in telling the story of who were the men and women and circumstances that formed this great king.

VO: For Nomsa Philiso, M-Net’s general entertainment CEO – the series HAD to be authentic.

NOMSA: It's an incredible story that reasserts our history // that will live for years to come so that our generations don't forget who they are and where they come.

LINK: Shaka iLembe – is a part of our heritage told by locals. But attempting to bring the pages of history alive requires vision, a big budget and guts.

NOMSA: Once in a while, every broadcaster takes a chance and says, You know what? I want to do something epic. And this was that for us

VO: It’s the biggest production budget in the history of MultiChoice.

Shaka Zulu was an ambitious man - with fierce determination and iron will, he conquered a nation with bravery, and at times, outright cruelty. A legacy that’s been contested throughout history.

UPSOUND SOMETHING WITH DIALOG
VO: Shot completely on location over six months – the Cradle of Humankind was the primary backdrop with four other locations in KwaZulu-Natal.

DESIREE: the cast was huge. // 250 actors on the show that had dialog.

UPSOUND

DESIREE: There were days that we had more than a thousand people on set in one day.

VO: Some of South Africa’s top actors joined forces in this mammoth production.

One of them is now Hollywood Movie Star, Nomzamo Mbatha who returned to South Africa for the role of King Shaka’s mother – Queen Nandi.

She is also one of the show’s executive producers.

NOMZAMO: it's legacy work that is truly spiritual. I can't even explain it. //you knew that you were creating something that was much greater than yourself.

VO: During the 12 part series – Mbatha transforms in her portrayal of Nandi, from a 16 year old maiden, to the young woman that gives birth to the ruler of the Zulu Kingdom, and stood firm as a Queen in her own right.

The role demanded stages of physical and emotional transformation.

NOTE FOR AUDIO MIX - CLAIRE AGREEING _ CUT OUT
NOMZAMO: //the performance side of it, how to be a young girl again, to be sassy like a young girl, to be cheeky /And then in the in the older woman, you know, she's she's had three children. // she's seen some things in her life, you know, and having to let go of any, you know, anything of of of self in that.

UPSOUND MOMENT…

LINK: When it comes to film making - it’s about creating scenes that are entertaining yet authentic – transporting audiences back in time to rural KwaZulu Natal in the 18th century was not going to be an easy feat.

UPSOUND… JUST A BREATH…

VO: A team of 120 experienced traditional hut builders constructed the set, with academics and historians, all weighing in, to create the most realistic scenes.

NOMSA: One of the things that I'm most proud about this project is that there was no international involvement in any shape or form. // everybody was South African which really was a proud moment for us, you know, to tell an African story with Africans.

VO: The cast were all in, refining their performances with the help of cultural and linguistic advisors - guiding them to deliver the most authentic versions of their characters.

NOMZAMO: // on a personal note, I was very insecure about dancing o and singing // And you have 200 people on set and everyone says And action. And it's Nandi in the center of everyone. And I have to be a young 16 year old girl is like, yeah, I know. Like, Oh, I can't do it. I could do it. So it really having to overcome the insecurity

UPSOUND DANCING CLIP

VO: Toiling amid the heat and dust the actors worked hard to deliver on the production team's vision of a world class TV series.

UPSOUND

VO: It's clear the series is lifted by not only the actors commitment to their jobs, but their connection to a profoundly and uniquely South African story about a warrior and king.

UPSOUND OF SCENE

DESIREE: // we wanted to approach it from a spiritual perspective, understanding that we needed to pay respects to the ancestors in the telling of the story. So even upfront at all our locations, we had a wonderful relationship with the Royal Praise Singer //

UPSOUND PRAISE SINGER

DESIREE: we really tried to invoke a sense within the whole crew and cast that this was not just a normal piece of television that we were making, but that we were telling an important history and that we wanted to acknowledge those who had come before us.

UPSOUND SCENE

VO: The entire series is filmed in isiZulu.

NOMZAMO: you want to be able to tell history in the in the most authentic way //so even in the slightest and smallest details. // we've got to be careful about how the body and the language is even being represented.

VO: Above all else, Shaka was a warrior and master military strategist. He developed battlefield tactics and weapons that were revolutionary. The battle scenes had to be extraordinary.

DESIREE: // where we had big battle scenes, we had three or 400 people on set. Many of those extras we pulled from dance communities // to choreograph how warriors would move in unison.

UPSOUND PRACTICE FIGHTING…

VO: But these scenes were carefully plotted, planned and practiced.

The end result is chilling….

UPSOUND FIGHT SCENES.

VO: Shaka is a story of betrayal, revenge, and violence. But it's also about courage and resilience.

NOMZAMO: I am very sure it will divide the audience and we're ready for it. It should be controversial.

VO: Shaka Ilembe is undeniably, a proud moment in the history of South African television.

DESIREE: //. It's really a love letter. It's a love gift to South Africans of just how beautiful this country is. And the talent that we have here.

UPSOUND CLIP SERIES

END





PROMOS

PROMO 1 – 21
UPSOUND….

VO: Six years in the making, Shaka iLembe is finally here – one of the biggest productions in South Africa television history.

NOMSA: Once ina while, every broadcaster takes a chance and says, You know what? I want to do something epic. And this was that for us


PROMO 2 – 21
VO: We go behind the scenes of Shaka iLembe and get a glimpse of how the magic was created.

NOMZAMO: it'slegacy work that is truly spiritual. I can't even explain it. //you knew that you were creating something that was much greater than yourself.

UPSOUND SERIES



PROMO 3 - 11
VO: We get a behind the scenes peak at the much anticipated Shaka iLembe – a historical drama series showcasing the best of African storytelling on an epic production scale.
